userStories.title: Union legacy memberships and baseline roles into effective keys
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make legacy membership and agent-role rows virtual permission bindings, with a baseline fallback and explicit invalidation API.

**Motivation** — `permissions-p1-roles` and `permissions-p1-membership` built the role model, but no route checks a permission key yet.

**Approach** — `PermissionService.computeKeys(principal, projectId)` gains two sources after the bindings and before the global-admin expansion:

1. **Legacy role keys.** A new `PrismaRoleBindingRepository.findLegacyRoleKeys(principal, projectId, agentScoping)` returns system role keys. It calls a new query `legacyRoleKeys(db, principal, projectId, agentScoping)` in `apps/api/src/permissions/legacy-membership.queries.ts`. For each returned key, `computeKeys` loads the role with `this.roles.findOne({ key })` and adds its entries the way it does for bindings. A key with no role row adds nothing.
   - `projectId` null: no keys.
   - USER: the user's `ProjectMember` row in the project answers `ROLE_KEY_FOR_LEGACY_ROLE[role]` for `ADMIN` and `DEVELOPER` (`project-admin`, `developer`) and `viewer` for any other stored role. No row: no keys.
   - AGENT, scoping on: `viewer` when the agent has an `AgentProject` row in the project. Then, when `agentHasProjectAccess(db, agentId, projectId)` is true (any access source, binding or legacy), one key per `AgentRoleEntry` role: `DEVELOPER` → `developer`, `REVIEWER` → `reviewer`, `VERIFIER` → `verifier`, `TRIAGER` → `triager`. An unknown stored role adds nothing.
   - AGENT, scoping off: `viewer` plus the `AgentRoleEntry` keys in every non-deleted project. This mirrors today's `AGENT_PROJECT_SCOPING=off`, where every agent reaches every project.
2. **Baseline fallback.** If the principal's bindings include no `projectId`-null binding of a GLOBAL-scope role, `computeKeys` adds the entries of `member` (USER) or `agent` (AGENT). Principals created before `permissions-p1-roles` have no baseline binding, and test fixtures write users and agents directly.

`agentScoping` is `authConfig.agentProjectScoping !== false`, the rule `AgentsService.agentScopingEnabled` uses. `PermissionService` gains a required fourth constructor parameter, `@Inject(AUTH_CFG) authConfig: IAuthConfig`.

**Cache.** The union results are cached with the binding keys under the existing `permissions` entries. A new `MembershipService.invalidatePermissions(): Promise<void>` calls `PermissionCache.invalidate()`. `AgentsService.updateRoles` calls it after its `AgentRoleEntry` write commits, so a role change takes effect on the next request. The other legacy writes either already go through `MembershipService` (member and roster removals) or happen only in tests.

**Global admins are unchanged:** a legacy `User.role = 'ADMIN'` user or a global `owner` or `admin` binding still holds every key in every project.

**The union also feeds anti-escalation.** `RoleAdminService` reads `PermissionService.effectiveKeys` as the caller's held set, so after this feature a legacy `ProjectMember` ADMIN row counts as `project-admin` there too (including `role.binding.manage` in that project), exactly as a `project-admin` binding does. This is intended: the union makes a legacy row equivalent to its mapped binding everywhere.

**Scope** — In: repository/query union, baseline fallback, fourth required authConfig argument, cache invalidation API, adapting all existing PermissionService constructions and in-memory binding doubles without changing previous assertions. Out: AgentsService.updateRoles production caller (US-009), route migration (US-003..US-010), catalog/seed edits (US-001), deleting compatibility rows/fallback, automatic invalidation for direct test fixture writes, and new tests for missing/unknown roles or invalid stored entries.

**Interface** — `findLegacyRoleKeys(principal, projectId, agentScoping): Promise<string[]>`; `legacyRoleKeys(db, principal, projectId, agentScoping): Promise<string[]>`; `MembershipService.invalidatePermissions(): Promise<void>`; `PermissionService(roles, bindings, cache, authConfig)`. Existing `can(principal, key, { projectId?, resource? })` and `effectiveKeys(principal, scope)` remain the authorization interfaces. Malformed role entries continue to add nothing and log a warning via existing addEntries; unknown agent roles or missing mapped/baseline roles add nothing. These excluded-test failure cases must not become new AC tests. Preserve repository-only Prisma access and current global-admin expansion.

userStories.title: Enforce ticket transition edge keys before writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce dedicated transition-route keys and current-status edge keys, including status PATCH preauthorization before field writes.

**Motivation** — A user bound to `reviewer` in a project gets the legacy `VIEWER` rights, because `legacyRoleForRoleKey` maps every role other than project-admin and developer to `VIEWER`.

**Approach** — New file `apps/api/src/tickets/state-machine/transition-keys.ts`:

```ts
/** The permission key of a state-machine edge; undefined for a pair with no key (not an edge, or the unreachable IN_PROGRESS -> VERIFIED). */
export function transitionKeyFor(from: TicketStatus, to: TicketStatus): string | undefined;

/** The key(s) that offer each allowedActions entry; an action is offered when the caller holds any of them. */
export const TICKET_ACTION_KEYS: Readonly<Record<TicketAction, readonly string[]>>;
```

| From | To | `transitionKeyFor` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| CREATED | VERIFIED | `ticket.transition.verify` |
| CREATED, VERIFIED | IN_PROGRESS | `ticket.transition.start` |
| CREATED, VERIFIED | REJECTED | `ticket.transition.reject` |
| IN_PROGRESS | VERIFY_FIX | `ticket.transition.fix` |
| VERIFY_FIX | CLOSED | `ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve` |
| VERIFY_FIX | IN_PROGRESS | `ticket.transition.verify-fix.return` |
| any other pair (including IN_PROGRESS → VERIFIED) | | `undefined` |

`TICKET_ACTION_KEYS`: `verify` → `[ticket.transition.verify]`, `start` → `[.start]`, `fix` → `[.fix]`, `verify-fix` → `[.verify-fix.approve, .verify-fix.return]`, `reject` → `[.reject]`, `close` → `[ticket.transition.close]`.

**The edge check.** `TicketTransitionsService.executeTransitionInternal`, after it loads the project and the ticket (the 404s) and before `validateTransition`, computes `transitionKeyFor(ticket.status, toStatus)`. When the key is defined and `permissions.can(principal, key, { projectId: project.id })` is not allowed, it throws 403 `permissions`. When the key is undefined, nothing is checked and `validateTransition` answers 400 as today. So `POST …/verify` on a `VERIFY_FIX` ticket (which `verify` turns into VERIFY_FIX → CLOSED) needs both `ticket.transition.verify` (the route) and `ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve` (the edge).

**`close`.** The close route's key (`ticket.transition.close`) is checked by `RequiresGuard` only; `TicketTransitionsService.close` adds no key check (no other caller reaches it). The controller's `canOverrideClose` call is removed.

**PATCH with `status`.** `TicketsService.update` no longer calls `assertTransitionPermission`. Before any field write it calls a new `TicketTransitionsService.assertTransitionAllowed(projectSlug, ref, toStatus, principal)`. That method loads the project and ticket (404s) and applies the same edge check, without validating the transition, so a refused edge still writes no field. `executeTransitionPublic` drops its `assertTransitionPermission` call, because `executeTransitionInternal` now checks the edge.

**Constructor.** `TicketTransitionsService` gains `PermissionService` as a **required third parameter**, after `txManager` and before the nine `@Optional()` parameters (`.nax/rules/api-core.md`: no `@Optional()` for a required dependency; TypeScript also forbids a required parameter after optional ones). Every positional construction inserts it as the third argument, shifting the rest by one. The `@Optional() caslAbilityFactory` stays last, used only by the legacy `assertTransitionPermission` (ruling 7).

Route keys, G=guard and S=edge service check:
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `PATCH …/tickets/:ref` | `ticket.update`; plus the edge key when `status` is sent | G + S (edge in `TicketTransitionsService`) | `@ProjectPermission(UPDATE)`, `assertTransitionPermission` |
| `POST …/:ref/verify`, `/start`, `/fix`, `/reject` | `ticket.transition.verify`, `.start`, `.fix`, `.reject`; plus the edge key | G + S (edge) | `@ProjectPermission(TRANSITION)` |
| `POST …/:ref/verify-fix` | `ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve` or `.return`, `mode: 'any'`; plus the edge key | G + S (edge) | `@ProjectPermission(TRANSITION)` |
| `POST …/:ref/close` | `ticket.transition.close` | G | `@ProjectPermission(TRANSITION)` + `canOverrideClose` |

Use ordered project+requires guards at the same level. Both route and defined edge must pass; do not mark the whole PATCH route service-only and lose ticket.update. Adapt existing metadata/CASL tests and every positional/DI construction listed in this story's modifiedFiles, preserving assistant assertTransitionPermission CASL assertions and unrelated PR/outbox/race/tenancy/indexing behavior.

**Scope** — In: transition-key mapping, action-key export for US-004, route metadata for PATCH and six transition routes, edge checks/precheck and required dependency migration. Out: remaining ticket CRUD routes and TicketsService constructor/allowedActions changes (US-004); assistant tool migration and changing assertTransitionPermission; deleting canOverrideClose or unreachable state-machine rule; reopen edges and fleet dispatch effect changes. TicketsService constructor is unchanged in this story.

**Interface** — The declarations above plus `assertTransitionAllowed(projectSlug: string, ref: string, toStatus: TicketStatus, principal: KodaPrincipal): Promise<void>`; `TicketTransitionsService(ticketRepo, txManager, permissions, ...nineOptionalParameters)`. Keep existing callable create/update/tool signatures. Undefined edges retain 400 tickets, defined-edge refusals answer 403 permissions before writes, and project/ticket lookups keep 404 precedence.

userStories.title: Enforce ticket CRUD keys and derive allowedActions per action
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Move ticket create/read/delete/assign routes onto keys and return only the status-valid actions the caller's edge keys allow.

**Motivation** — And any agent on a roster can still create and delete tickets and manage labels whatever its role, which the 2026-10-18 review flagged (ruling 2).

**Approach** — `allowedActions(status, permitted)` in `apps/api/src/tickets/state-machine/allowed-actions.ts` changes its second parameter from `{ canTransition, canClose }` to `permitted: ReadonlySet<TicketAction>`. An action is returned when it is valid from `status` (the existing `ACTION_TARGETS` and `CLOSE_SOURCES` rules) and is in `permitted`. `TicketsService.findByRefWithActions` builds `permitted` as the actions whose `TICKET_ACTION_KEYS` entry has at least one key `can` allows in the ticket's project. `TicketsService` replaces its `KodaCaslAbilityFactory` constructor parameter with `PermissionService`, in the same position (US-004). Its `update` change (calling `assertTransitionAllowed`) is US-003's and needs no new `TicketsService` dependency.

Route keys:
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /projects/:slug/tickets` | `ticket.create` | G | `@ProjectPermission(CREATE Ticket)` |
| `GET /projects/:slug/tickets`, `GET …/tickets/:ref` | `ticket.read` | G | guard only |
| `DELETE …/tickets/:ref` | `ticket.delete` | G | `@ProjectPermission(DELETE)` |
| `POST …/tickets/:ref/assign` | `ticket.assign` | G | `@ProjectPermission(UPDATE)` |

`TICKET_ACTION_KEYS`: `verify` → `[ticket.transition.verify]`, `start` → `[.start]`, `fix` → `[.fix]`, `verify-fix` → `[.verify-fix.approve, .verify-fix.return]`, `reject` → `[.reject]`, `close` → `[ticket.transition.close]`.

Every project route has `ProjectMembershipGuard` before `RequiresGuard` in one guard declaration at the same level. Keep US-003's PATCH ticket.update/edge checks. Remove migrated legacy decorators, not shared legacy factories/helpers. Preserve the ordering of actions and strict state-machine comment-type validity. A ReadonlySet filters valid actions; it must not make fix valid from CREATED.

Update existing tickets.service/controller and allowed-actions specs to key-based doubles and metadata. Developer on CREATED now receives ['verify','start','reject']; Reviewer on CREATED receives []. Pass permissions rather than a CASL factory in the manual TicketsService construction in integration/memory/outbox-envelope.integration.spec.ts while preserving envelope assertions. The project-role integration allowedActions row must include every status-valid action Developer holds. The existing endpoint.e2e.spec.ts Agent Permissions block first restores roles to ['DEVELOPER'] through PATCH /api/agents/:slug/update-roles after the earlier REVIEWER change; label-create remains 201, agent ticket-delete becomes 403 permissions, and a project-admin caller deletes the ticket. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply catalog keys to comments, labels, ticket labels and watchers, with row ownership checked through can.

**Motivation** — This feature makes the seeded roles real on the core surface: a principal can do on a core route exactly what its keys allow.

**Approach** — **Comments.** `CommentsService.update` and `delete` keep `assertCommentProjectMembership` (a non-member still gets 404). | Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST …/:ref/comments` | `comment.create` | G | guard only |
| `GET …/:ref/comments` | `comment.read` | G | guard only |
| `PATCH /comments/:id` | `comment.update` | S (`CommentsService.update`, ownership) | `@RequiredPermission(UPDATE Comment)` + CASL |
| `DELETE /comments/:id` | `comment.delete` | S (`CommentsService.delete`, ownership) | `@RequiredPermission(DELETE Comment)` + CASL |

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist nullable ticket-link creators and enforce add/read/own-or-full removal keys without changing the link response contract.

**Motivation** — This feature makes the seeded roles real on the core surface: a principal can do on a core route exactly what its keys allow.

**Approach** — **Links.** `TicketLinksService.remove(slug, ref, linkId, principal)` gains the principal. After it finds the link (404 `ticket-links` when absent), it calls `can(principal, 'ticket.link.remove', { projectId, resource: { createdBy } })` with the link's creator. `TicketLinksService` gains `PermissionService` as a required last constructor parameter.

- **Schema.** `TicketLink` gains two nullable columns, `createdByUserId String?` and `createdByAgentId String?`, with no foreign key and no index (like `JobSchedule.repoId`, the value is compared and never joined). A new Prisma migration adds them. Existing rows keep null.
- **Writes.** `TicketLinksService.create(slug, ref, dto, createdBy?: PrincipalRef)` gains an optional last parameter. When it is given and a new link is created, it records `createdByUserId` or `createdByAgentId`. An existing link returned with status 200 is not changed. `POST …/links` passes the caller. The assistant's link tool and the VCS and fleet writers do not pass it, so their links have no creator, and only holders of the full `ticket.link.remove` key (Project Admin, global admins) can remove them.
- **Response.** `TicketLinkResponseDto` is unchanged. The creator is not exposed.

- The ticket links controller drops `assertMembership` and its `ProjectsService` dependency. The guards cover it.

| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST …/:ref/links`, `GET …/:ref/links` | `ticket.link.add`, `ticket.link.read` | G | controller `assertMembership` |
| `DELETE …/:ref/links/:linkId` | `ticket.link.remove` | S (`TicketLinksService.remove`, ownership) | controller `assertMembership` |

Use ordered project+requires guards. Removal carries `@Requires('ticket.link.remove', { enforcedBy: 'service' })` and authorizes after scoped ticket/link lookup, so unknown links retain 404 ticket-links and non-members retain guard 403 projects. Creator references use USER/AGENT discriminants and matching id; neither creator yields null and cannot satisfy own-only removal. Persist and map the fields through PrismaTicketLinkRepository.createLink/toDomain and TicketLinkDomain. Migration path: apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261028090000_ticket_link_creator/migration.sql. Regenerate the Prisma client, not generated API clients by hand. Update constructor/remove call sites in link specs and the cross-project tenancy integration; preserve scoped ref and missing-resource assertions. Controller tests no longer assert its own membership method calls; provide ProjectAccessService and PermissionService doubles for the guards, verify caller is passed on create/remove.

**Scope** — In: creator schema/migration/domain mapping, additive optional creator writes, link route and service authorization. Out: comment ownership (US-005), ticket CRUD/transitions (US-003/004), changing assistant/VCS/fleet writers, exposing creator DTO fields or backfilling existing links.

**Interface** — `create(slug, ref, dto, createdBy?: PrincipalRef)`; `remove(slug, ref, linkId, principal)`; `TicketLinksService(repo, permissions)`; `TicketLinksController(ticketLinksService)`. The REST create handler converts its KodaPrincipal into a PrincipalRef with type USER for a user or AGENT for an agent and the same id; it must not pass the raw actorType-shaped principal as the optional creator. Removal receives the full KodaPrincipal for PermissionService.can. TicketLink carries `createdByUserId: string | null` and `createdByAgentId: string | null` internally only.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply global agent-management keys, authorize pickup using the target agent's project keys and make role changes visible on the next request.

**Motivation** — And any agent on a roster can still create and delete tickets and manage labels whatever its role, which the 2026-10-18 review flagged (ruling 2).

**Approach** — - `AgentsService.suggestTicket` keeps its owning-agent-or-global-admin check and its agent and project lookups. After the project lookup, the roster check (scoping on) is replaced by a check on the **target agent**: `(await permissions.effectiveKeys({ type: 'AGENT', id: agent.id }, { projectId })).has('agent.pickup')`, 403 `permissions` when false. This keeps today's meaning: the pickup is the target agent's act in the project, so a global ADMIN caller cannot pick up for an agent that holds no `agent.pickup` there (with scoping on, an agent with no source in the project holds no project key). `AgentsService` gains `PermissionService` as a required fifth constructor parameter, after `membership` and before the two `@Optional()` parameters.
- `AgentsService.updateRoles` calls `membership.invalidatePermissions()` after its write.
- `GET /agents/me` refuses a non-agent principal with 403 `agents` in the controller (the old `AgentScope` check answered a generic 403).

Route keys:
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `POST /agents` | `agent.create` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /agents`, `GET /agents/:slug` | `agent.read` | G | none |
| `GET /agents/me` | `agent.self.read` | G (implicit) + agents-only check in the controller | `@RequiredPermission(READ AgentScope)` |
| `GET /agents/:slug/pickup` | `agent.pickup` (held by the target agent) | S (`AgentsService.suggestTicket`, after the project lookup) | self-or-admin check (kept); roster check |
| `PATCH /agents/:slug`, `…/update-roles`, `…/update-capabilities`, `DELETE /agents/:slug`, `POST …/rotate-key` | `agent.update`, `agent.roles.update`, `agent.capabilities.update`, `agent.delete`, `agent.key.rotate` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |

Missing project query still gives 400 agents in the controller; self-or-admin refusal remains 403 agents before agent/project lookup. Target-agent effectiveKeys is required even for a global admin caller and even when scoping is off; US-002 provides scoping-off project roles. Global management keys must not be satisfied by project-admin. Keep credential-route throttle and auth-cache invalidation. Permission invalidation occurs after the AgentRoleEntry write commits, so the following ticket.create request observes the new role.

Adapt all constructor/TestingModule seams and membership doubles listed in this story's modifiedFiles, including GlobalStubsModule.invalidatePermissions. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish core declarations on global admin routes and public/implicit routes while retaining existing authentication and principal-type rules.

**Motivation** — This feature makes the seeded roles real on the core surface: a principal can do on a core route exactly what its keys allow.

**Approach** — Route keys:
| Route | Key | | Replaces |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `GET /admin/users`, `POST`, `PATCH …/:id` | `user.read`, `user.create`, `user.update` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `GET /admin/outbox`, `POST /admin/outbox/:eventId/retry`, `GET /admin/slos` | `outbox.read`, `outbox.retry`, `admin.slo.read` | G | `@RequiredPermission('ADMIN')` |
| `POST /auth/register`, `GET /auth/registration-status`, `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh` | `auth.register`, `auth.registration.read`, `session.login`, `session.refresh` | G (public) | `@Public()` (kept) |
| `GET /auth/me`, `POST /auth/logout`, `GET /home` | `auth.me.read`, `session.logout`, `home.read` | G (implicit) | none |
| `GET /me/notifications`, `…/unread-count`, `POST /me/notifications/:id/read`, `POST …/read-all`, `GET /me/notification-preferences`, `PUT …` | `notification.read`, `notification.read`, `notification.mark-read`, `notification.mark-read`, `notification.preference.read`, `notification.preference.update` | G (implicit) | users-only check (kept) |
| `GET /invites/:token`, `POST /invites/:token/accept` | `invite.preview`, `invite.accept` | G (public) | `@Public()` (kept) |

Global routes (no slug) have `RequiresGuard` only. Public routes retain @Public and existing throttling; refresh also keeps JwtRefreshGuard, because a public catalog declaration is not refresh-token authentication. Implicit keys require an authenticated principal but do not replace controller principal-type/domain checks. The home and /me notification routes keep refusing agents. Auth me still answers 401 auth for an agent because its handler finds no user row. Keep admin self-demotion's 403 users.self, other domain rules and DTO response mapping. Replace only legacy RequiredPermission gates on listed routes.

Move the admin users, outbox and SLO routes onto global keys, and declare the public and implicit keys on the auth (`auth.controller.ts`), home (`home/home.controller.ts`), `/me` notification (`notifications/me-notifications.controller.ts`) and public invite (`projects/invites/public-invites.controller.ts`) routes. Their existing principal-type refusals (home and notifications refuse agents) are kept.

Adapt admin-users.controller.spec.ts to REQUIRES_METADATA user.read/create/update, UsersModule fake globals to provide PermissionService, and outbox/auth controller harnesses for RequiresGuard DI while preserving handler assertions. Route integration ACs verify allow/refuse outcomes rather than adding a full catalog contract test or new endpoint e2e cases.

**Scope** — In: the listed admin/auth/home/notification/public invite route declarations and removal of their replaced legacy gates. Out: agent-only /agents/me (US-009), project invite management (US-008), project/ticket route migration (US-003..US-007), fleet/integration authorization, unlisted live/SSE routes and changing authentication/session semantics.

**Interface** — `@Requires(key)` and `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)` use US-001's guard metadata, without new service signatures. Public keys pass without principal; implicit keys pass only after authentication, then existing handler-level restrictions still decide their own error codes. No API response DTO contract changes are introduced.

Folding or removing the catalog keys the design marks as removed (`project.agent.add`, `project.agent.update`, `project.agent.remove`, `member.role.update`, `agent.roles.update`, `fleet.approval.decide.*`) is out of scope (`permissions-p1-cleanup`). This feature uses them on their routes.

Deleting the unreachable IN_PROGRESS → VERIFIED rule from `TRANSITION_RULES` is out of scope (`permissions-p1-cleanup`). `transitionKeyFor` gives it no key, and no route reaches it.
A reopen edge (CLOSED or REJECTED back to an open status) is out of scope (design decision: no reopen edge).
Approval of any action (`approvalMode`, `ApprovalRequest`, policies) is out of scope (P3). A permitted request runs immediately.
Recording an actor context or audit entry for these writes is out of scope (P2).
Web changes are out of scope (`permissions-p1-web`). The web reads `allowedActions`, `canManage` and the 403 responses as before.

Rewriting the stored permissions of an existing database's unlocked system roles with the new `!project.ci-token.read` and `!invite.read` entries is out of scope. The seeder writes them when it creates a role, and koda-wk is reset when P1 ships.
Exposing a ticket link's creator in `TicketLinkResponseDto`, and backfilling the creator of existing links, are out of scope.

Invalidating the permission cache when a test fixture writes a legacy `ProjectMember`, `AgentProject` or `AgentRoleEntry` row directly is out of scope. Only `PATCH /agents/:slug/update-roles` writes `AgentRoleEntry` in production, and it invalidates.
